properties.title: FeO Abundance · Kaguya MI 65N-65S (Shi et al. 2026)
properties.authors: Shi X., Chen J., Wang J., Liu S., Tong X., Li J., Yan Z., Wen S., Xie H., He Z., Chu J., Hu W., Wang F.
properties.producer_institution_name: Tongji University; Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
properties.crs: Source: 9 GeoTIFFs of 20480 x 66560 px, geographic GCS_Moon_2000 in degrees on the 1737400 m sphere. COG: the 9 joined, IAU:30100, same sphere and grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Kaguya Multiband Imager level 5 reflectance after terrain shadow correction (8 bands, 415 to 1550 nm) and the spectral angles θTi and θFe, inverted with a residual 1D CNN (Res-CNN). Leave-one-out training on 56 samples from Apollo, Luna, Chang'E-5, and Chang'e-6 sites gives 56 models whose weights are averaged. Distributed as 9 Float32 GeoTIFFs of 40° longitude, 65N to 65S, 512 ppd, values in wt%, clipped to 0 to 24 wt% between 180°W and 60°E. COG: gdalbuildvrt joins the 9 files (one grid, no resampling); gdal_calc.py maps the source NoData (3.4e38) to -9999; gdal_translate assigns IAU:30100 and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Higher FeO indicates mare basalt; ilmenite-associated FeO is a target for oxygen extraction. Resolves individual craters and lava flows at 59 m/pixel between 65N and 65S.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Res-CNN FeO from Kaguya MI, calibrated with Chang'e-6 samples, 59 m/pixel, 65N-65S. RMSE 0.22 wt% at the training sites. Orbit stripes in places; NoData along orbit gaps; values at 0 and 24 wt% mostly artifacts.
properties.lri:quality_note: RMSE 0.22 wt% between map and measured values at the 56 training sites; R² 0.98 and RMSE 1.99 wt% over the six oxides at held-out test sites (Supplementary Table 4). Pixel mean 8.32 wt%, equal to the article's global mean (8.30 wt%). Between 180°W and 60°E, values are clipped to 0 to 24 wt% (0.014% of valid pixels at 0, 0.144% at 24); east of 60°E almost no pixel is at either end. The authors give 24 wt% as the maximum of the FeO inversion; the training samples span 4.2 to 22.6 wt%. Most pixels at 0 or 24 wt% are artifacts. Bands at 24 wt%, a few km wide, line orbit gaps, mostly at 20 to 60°E; patches at 0 and 24 wt% cover steep slopes poleward of 55°, with 15 to 23 wt% around them in highland of about 5 wt%; 84% of the pixels at 0 wt% lie there. The median FeO around pixels at 24 wt% is 11 wt%. Mare FeO is 1 to 3.5 wt% above the Lucey-algorithm FeO of Speyerer et al. (2023); highland values agree within about 1 wt%. NoData covers 1.69% of pixels, mostly in gaps along orbit tracks, and up to 21% of each column within 0.2° west and 0.4° east of 180°. North-south stripes about 1.06° apart, the longitude step between successive Kaguya orbits, appear at 20 to 35°E and 55 to 100°E and more weakly at 110 to 135°W and near 165°E; column means deviate from their 1° running median by up to 2 wt%. The source is 9 files of 40° longitude. At 180° the two sides do not match pixel for pixel (mean step +0.14 wt%); at 60°E the mean step is -0.01 wt%; the other boundaries are continuous. Registered to the LRO frame: at 10 of 12 landing sites the offset to Speyerer et al. (2023) FeO, registered to the LROC WAC mosaic, is within 0.3 km.
